name: VocalBench
ability_definition: The ability to communicate information and ideas in speaking so others will understand.

task_realism.reasoning: Tasks are spoken responses to spoken queries covering knowledge, reasoning, creative, instruction-following, emotional and safety prompts. This loosely resembles answering questions or explaining ideas aloud. It lacks workplace-typical oral tasks such as briefing a team, instructing a coworker, handling a customer call, or presenting findings to a specific audience.

evaluation_conditions.reasoning: Mostly short, single-exchange interactions graded by automated proxies (LLM judge on transcripts, UTMOS, Whisper WER). No real listener checks comprehension, and there are no stakes, no audience-specific context, and little extended back-and-forth. The robustness dimension (noise and channel perturbations) adds some realism about input conditions.

construct_coverage.reasoning: It measures both what is said (semantic quality, coherence) and how it is said (acoustic naturalness, speech-content consistency), which covers the two core pillars of the ability. It does not directly measure whether listeners actually understood. It also misses adaptation to audience expertise, sustained multi-minute explanation, and interactive clarification when understanding breaks down.

format_match.reasoning: Inputs and outputs are real audio speech, the same modality as workplace oral communication, rather than multiple choice or text proxies. However, the clips are short curated prompts in a benchmark-style Q&A format, not natural workplace conversations or presentations.

transferability_reasoning: VocalBench is a genuine speech-in/speech-out evaluation that jointly scores content and delivery, so it targets the right construct better than reasoning-focused or read-aloud TTS benchmarks. Transfer is limited because listener understanding is judged by automated tools rather than humans. Its short, curated single-exchange prompts also fail to capture audience adaptation, extended explanation, and interactive repair, which are central to workplace oral communication.

2025.metric: VocalBench overall composite score (0-100 scale, aggregated across semantic, acoustic, chat and robustness sub-metrics)
2025.human_reference: General adult workforce who communicate orally at work: typical employees answering questions, explaining information and following spoken requests in conversation.
